nodes.label: Load Balancer
nodes.about: Picks a server from a hash of the short code, so the same code always lands on the same server while the pool is unchanged.

nodes.label: API 1
nodes.when_down: Its share of codes re-hashes onto the other servers.

nodes.label: API 2
nodes.when_down: Its share of codes re-hashes onto the other servers.

nodes.label: API 3
nodes.when_down: Its share of codes re-hashes onto the other servers.

nodes.label: Redis
nodes.about: Two jobs: caches code → URL for fast redirects, and counts requests per client for rate limiting.
nodes.when_down: Redirects fall back to the database replicas. Creating links fails, because the rate limiter can't count.

nodes.label: Postgres primary
nodes.about: Takes every write. Reads go to the replicas.
nodes.when_down: No new links can be created, but redirects keep working from the replicas.

nodes.label: Replica 1
nodes.about: A read-only copy of the primary.

nodes.label: Replica 2
nodes.about: A read-only copy of the primary.

shorten.say: Rate limit: count this client's requests (5 allowed)

scenarios.label: Redis is down
scenarios.explain: Redirects skip the cache and read a replica. Reads scale by adding replicas, not by touching the primary.

scenarios.label: Primary is down
scenarios.explain: Reads only need a replica, so redirects survive the primary failing. Creating a link now fails: try it.

scenarios.label: Can't create without primary
scenarios.explain: Writes have exactly one place to go. That is why a primary failure needs a failover plan.

scenarios.label: Both replicas down
scenarios.explain: With no replicas left, reads fall back to the primary, which now carries all the load.

scenarios.label: API 2 down
scenarios.explain: Hashing over the live servers moves this code to another server. With plain hashing many codes move at once; consistent hashing limits that.
